closure_distance_reason: The new finite exclusions do not cover arbitrary A or length, and the length-independent invariants admit integral nonbacktracking composite closed walks.
new_results: Complete enumeration of 734,320,442 multiplier tuples in the stated fixed-(A,length) domains, with no nonbacktracking prime closed walk.
Consequent exclusion of fixed-A bicyclic cores with total edges <=9 for A=4, <=6 for A=8, <=4 for A=16, and <=3 for A=32 or 64.
Length-independent fixed-A cycle identities sum p_i=sum q_i and equality of the two Euler products with product(h_i)/A^m.
Strict-concavity crossing lemma: unequal p/q multisets in a fixed-A cycle must be incomparable in majorization order.
Exact A=4 composite nonbacktracking counterwalk showing the new identities alone cannot exclude cycles.

first_unfixable_breakpoint: Control two fixed- or mixed-valuation cycles simultaneously along their shared path; single-cycle Euler products and first moments permit crossing composite walks.
route_killed: Euler-product equality, even when combined with the first moment, does not force an integral closed walk to backtrack.
next_decidable_action: Subtract the two cycle identities on theta shared paths and test whether primality forces compatible majorization directions; otherwise construct the first all-prime crossing bicyclic core.
quantifier_warning: Even a complete semiprime proper-neighbour Hall theorem would still require prime-square, higher-odd-part and matching-union arguments before settling the original exact extremal problem.
